stories.headline: 3 books of Kashmiri poet Dr A H Shah released
stories.title: 3 books of Kashmiri poet Dr A H Shah released
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 24: In a significant celebration of Kashmir's literary heritage and intellectual tradition, three books authored by Dr. A.H. Shah were formally released by Minister for Youth Services and Sports Mir Saifullah, at an impressive literary and academic function held at the Auditorium of Teachers Bhavan, Bemina, Srinagar. The programme was organised by Al-Anwar Academy, Kashmir, in collaboration with Shahbaz Cultural Forum, with the principal objective of commemorating the extraordinary literary legacy of eminent Kashmiri poet Ali Muhammad Shahbaz of Mawar, Kupwara, and bringing his poetic vision to a wider readership through translation, critical interpretation and scholarly engagement. The proceedings commenced with a welcome address by Er. G.M. War, Convenor, Al-Anwar Academy, Kashmir, who articulated the Academy's intellectual vision and its commitment to promoting literary scholarship, academic discourse and knowledge-oriented initiatives. He emphasised that the preservation, documentation and dissemination of Kashmir's literary heritage constitute an essential responsibility towards safeguarding the region's cultural identity and intellectual legacy. He also outlined the Academy's forthcoming literary and academic initiatives aimed at fostering a vibrant culture of reading, research and intellectual engagement. The two significant publications, Raho Rasme Shahbazi and Lore of the Falcon, represent a noteworthy scholarly endeavour to retrieve, interpret and disseminate the literary contributions of Ali Muhammad Shahbaz. Both volumes contain literary translations of his Kashmiri poetry, enriched with scholarly annotations, explanatory notes and critical observations. Together, they offer valuable insights into the aesthetic refinement, philosophical depth, revolutionary spirit and socio-cultural consciousness embedded in Shahbaz's poetic expression. The translations have received considerable appreciation from academicians, literary critics and readers, providing an opportunity to engage with the poet's creative universe beyond the linguistic boundaries of Kashmiri. The publications constitute a meaningful contribution to the preservation and international accessibility of Kashmir's literary heritage. The third publication, Cricket in the Conifers, further reflects Dr. A.H. Shah's diverse literary interests and intellectual engagement, adding another dimension to his creative and scholarly pursuits. Addressing the gathering, Minister Mir Saifullah appreciated the commendable initiative undertaken by Al-Anwar Academy, Kashmir, and Shahbaz Cultural Forum in bringing the literary achievements of Ali Muhammad Shahbaz into wider public and academic consciousness. He observed that Shahbaz deserved a more prominent and enduring place in Kashmir's literary history, considering the exceptional depth, lyrical cadence, emotional intensity and evocative power of his poetry. He underscored the importance of recognising distinguished literary personalities whose creative contributions form an inseparable part of Kashmir's cultural and intellectual inheritance. The function was presided over by Justice Bashir Kirmani. Former Member of Parliament and noted political personality Sharif-ud-Din Shariq was among the distinguished personalities present. The presidium also comprised Padma Shri Professor Shafi Shouq and former Secretary of the Jammu and Kashmir Academy of Art, Culture and Languages, Zafar Iqbal Manhas. A significant academic dimension was added to the proceedings through scholarly presentations examining the literary, philosophical and intellectual aspects of the publications. Professor Hamid Nasim Rafiabadi and Dr. Sohan Lal Koul, renowned author and literary critic, presented insightful papers. Dr. Sohan Lal Koul, in particular, delivered an engaging and critically nuanced paper on Raho Rasme Shahbazi and Lore of the Falcon, offering an illuminating assessment of their literary significance, interpretative depth and contribution to the preservation of Kashmir's poetic tradition. His scholarly observations enriched the deliberations and provided a deeper critical perspective on the translated works. A panel discussion on the translated publications and the literary stature of Ali Muhammad Shahbaz was subsequently held under the chairmanship of Professor Shafi Shouq and moderated by Dr. G.M. Khan. The panel included Professor Majrooh Rashid, Professor Nasir Mirza and Professor Jehangir, besides other distinguished scholars. During the deliberations, speakers observed that Ali Muhammad Shahbaz occupies a considerably more significant position in Kashmir's literary history than has generally been acknowledged. His revolutionary and romantic poetry, distinguished by intellectual vigour, emotional intensity, imaginative richness and an unmistakable literary cadence, continues to retain its relevance and appeal. They highlighted the remarkable synthesis of literary excellence, cultural consciousness, humanistic values and creative resistance reflected in his poetic oeuvre. The participants particularly appreciated the intellectual initiative of translating Shahbaz's poetry, observing that literary translation is not merely a linguistic exercise but an important instrument of cultural transmission, critical interpretation and civilisational dialogue. Such initiatives enable regional literary voices to transcend linguistic limitations and become accessible to wider national and international audiences. The occasion witnessed an impressive gathering of eminent academicians, celebrated literary personalities, cultural activists, members of the judiciary and representatives of civil society, reflecting the intellectual significance and cultural resonance of the programme. The programme concluded with a collective resolve to sustain initiatives in literary research, translation, documentation and critical scholarship, ensuring that the creative achievements of distinguished Kashmiri writers and poets receive their rightful recognition in the broader literary discourse. The release of these three publications was widely regarded as more than a conventional literary event; it represented a meaningful intellectual intervention towards rediscovering Kashmir's literary inheritance, strengthening its cultural consciousness and carrying the creative legacy of Ali Muhammad Shahbaz to future generations.

stories.headline: Days before Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice’s retirement, Supreme Court Collegium proposes successor
stories.title: Days before Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice’s retirement, Supreme Court Collegium proposes successor
stories.summary: The Collegium’s decision has come shortly after Chief Minister Hemant Soren wrote to Chief Justice of India, expressing concern about a lack of decision regarding a successor to Justice Sonak, superannuating on November 27
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
event term: 'chief justice' in summary weight 25.2
event term: 'chief justice of india' in summary weight 27.6
article_sentences: Hardly three days before the retirement of incumbent Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice M.S. Sonak, the Supreme Court Collegium headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) proposed the transfer of Karnataka High Court Chief Vibhu Bakhru to the office.

The Collegium’s decision has come shortly after Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Sorenwrote to the Chief Justice of India, expressing concern about a lack of decision regarding a successor to Justice Sonak, who is superannuating on November 27.

Mr. Soren had highlighted that a Chief Justice to the State High Court should ideally have been recommended by the Supreme Court Collegium in advance, and cleared by the Union government as per the Memorandum of Procedure for appointment of judges to the constitutional courts.

The Chief Minister, as the head of the State government had expressed objections about any interim arrangement, making it clear that the State High Court must have a regular Chief Justice at the helm.

Mr. Soren, in his letter to the CJI and the Collegium judges, had reportedly pointed out that frequent transitions accompanied by extended interim arrangements disrupt administrative continuity, affect institutional planning and create uncertainty within the judicial establishment.
On Tuesday (November 24), the Supreme Court Collegium proposed that Justice Bakhru take over as Chief Justice of Jharkhand High Court upon the retirement of the incumbent Chief Justice.
The ball is now with the government to clear the Collegium resolution and notify the appointment of Justice Bakhru by November 27.
The Collegium has recommended Justice M.S. Ramachandra Rao, the Chief Justice of Tripura High Court, to be transferred as the Chief Justice of the Karnataka High Court in the place of Justice Bakhru.

In a separate resolution on November 24, the Collegium recommended the appointment of Himachal Pradesh High Court judge, Justice Vivek Singh Thakur, as Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court following the transfer of Justice Rao to Karnataka High Court.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Collegium Recommends Justice Vibhu Bakhru As Jharkhand HC Chief Justice, Justice Ramachandra Rao For Karnataka HC
stories.title: Supreme Court Collegium Recommends Justice Vibhu Bakhru As Jharkhand HC Chief Justice, Justice Ramachandra Rao For Karnataka HC
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
article_sentences: The Supreme Court Collegium, headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, has recommended the transfer of Justice Vibhu Bakhru, Chief Justice of the Karnataka High Court, as the Chief Justice of the Jharkhand High Court.
The Collegium has also recommended the transfer of Justice M.S. Ramachandra Rao, Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court, as the Chief Justice of the Karnataka High Court.
The recommendations were made at a Collegium meeting held on November 24, 2026.
Justice Bakhru's transfer to the Jharkhand High Court is consequent upon the retirement of the incumbent Chief Justice of the High Court on November 27, 2026.
Justice Bakhru was elevated as a judge of the Delhi High Court in 2013.
He was appointed as the Chief Justice of the Karnataka High Court in 2025.
Justice M.S. Ramachandra Rao, who hails from the Telangana High Court, was appointed as the Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court.
He has previously served as a judge of the Telangana and Andhra Pradesh High Courts.

stories.headline: Indian Student In Russia Joins Russian Army; Supreme Court Seeks Centre's Response On Father's Plea For His Return
stories.title: Indian Student In Russia Joins Russian Army; Supreme Court Seeks Centre's Response On Father's Plea For His Return
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Considering an Indian father's plea for repatriation of his son, who apparently went to Russia on a student visa and then got enrolled in the Russian Army, the Supreme Court recently called on the Union of India to consider intervention in the matter on humanitarian grounds.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana passed the order in the petitioner-father's plea, asking Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to intervene in the matter obtain instructions.
The bench considered that only limited intervention by the Indian authorities was possible, as the petitioner's son had seemingly relinquished his Indian citizenship and acquired Russian citizenship.

The SG however informed the bench that the Russian authorities had informed the Indian Embassy that the petitioner's son had taken Russian citizenship, and hence the scope for Indian intervention was limited.
The matter has been posted to January, 2027.
Briefly put, the petitioner has two sons.
The son stated to be stuck in Russia - Abinesh - is his younger son, who apparently travelled to Russia in April with 3 other students on student visa.
Abinesh travelled to Russia taking the assistance of an agent he found on Instagram.
After he went to Russia, the petitioner and other family members could contact him last on July 19.
After that, they could not get in direct contact with Abinesh (or the 3 other students).
Concerned about his safety, Abinesh's elder brother accessed his email account and found certain documents, including a Russian Army ID/military tag.

As it appeared that Abinesh may have become a Russian citizen and got enrolled in the Russian Army, his family raised a grievance before the Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India requesting immediate intervention.

stories.headline: Keralam sanctions ₹1,089 cr for November welfare pensions; distribution begins Wednesday
stories.title: Keralam sanctions ₹1,089 cr for November welfare pensions; distribution begins Wednesday
stories.summary: Chief Minister V D Satheesan says Kerala has sanctioned ₹1,088.63 crore for November pensions, with distribution to over 65 lakh beneficiaries beginning Wednesday.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Chief Minister V D Satheesan on Tuesday said the state government had sanctioned ₹1,088.63 crore for November’s social security and welfare board pensions, benefiting more than 65 lakh people.
He added that the distribution of the amount would begin on Wednesday.
Of the total, ₹964.41 crore has been allocated for social security pensions and ₹124.22 crore for welfare board pensions, Satheesan said in a Facebook post.
He said pension payments had been made without interruption for the seventh consecutive month since the UDF came to power.
“The government’s objective is to ensure that eligible beneficiaries receive their pensions on time,” he added.
